sections.h2: Where a Washington County deed gets recorded
sections.html:
Take the deed to the Recorder of Deeds in the Crossroads Center, 95 W. Beau St., Suite 520, Washington, PA 15301. The number is 724-228-6806. Staff work until 4:30 p.m., but the recording window shuts at 4:00 p.m. Plan around 4:00.

The office has existed since 1781, when the county was cut out of Westmoreland County. It records deeds, mortgages, subdivision plans and other papers the state treats as permanent, takes in the fees and taxes that come with them, and splits the receipts among the commonwealth, county, townships and boroughs, and school boards. Everything is indexed, verified and scanned the same business day.

A Washington County sale ends at this counter. After the deed is signed at closing it is filed here, and the buyer becomes the owner of record. Landex, an online search, holds every deed back to 1781, and terminals in the office let you look up what sits on a property. Landex support is 1-800-370-2836, option 4.

What you pay first depends on the document type. Each base fee already includes four pages, four indexed names and one PIN. A schedule and a calculator sit on the recorder's web page, so run your numbers there before cutting a check.

Extras beyond the base recording fee
Add-onCharge
Included in base fee4 pages, 4 indexed names, 1 PIN
Each additional page$2.00
Each additional indexed name$0.50
Each additional PIN$10.00
CJEA surchargeRaised from $2.50 to $3.50

The printed schedule can lag behind the $1 CJEA increase, so a schedule you find online may show a total $1 lower than what the counter collects. If the total is unclear, call 724-228-6806 before you send payment.

Two details catch people out. The PIN charge applies per parcel number, so a sale that combines several parcels costs more than a single-lot sale. And the extra-page charge adds up on long documents, such as a deed with a full legal description and several exhibits.

Legally, both buyer and seller. The state realty transfer tax is 1 percent of the transfer value, and Harrisburg treats grantor and grantee as jointly and severally liable, which lets it collect the full amount from either one.

The recorder takes the state share plus, usually, a local share, and forwards both. Local money is divided between the county, the municipality and the school district, so the rate depends on where the house stands. Ask the recorder or the closing agent for the combined rate before you decide what you will net.

  • Some transfers are exempt: certain ones between relatives, some to government bodies, and inheritance under a will or without one.
  • Claiming an exemption usually takes a form, which the office can name.
  • The sale contract sets who actually pays. The recorder stays out of that.

sections.h2: Formatting rules that get documents rejected
sections.html:
Page size and type size are the two rules the county stresses. Legal-size pages are no longer taken electronically, and there are minimum fonts: 12 point on letter-size pages and 14 point on legal-size pages.

Subdivision plans follow their own rules. They are filed on paper or mylar, and they need signatures from the Washington County Planning Commission, the local planning commission where one applies, the board of supervisors or borough council, and the owners of the land being divided. The plan also carries an engineer's seal, and recording must happen inside 90 days of the local governing body's approval.

  • Check page size before you scan a deed for e-recording.
  • Confirm the type size on a long exhibit, because tiny print often gets a filing bounced.
  • For a plan, count the 90 days from the local approval, rather than from the day the drawings are finished.

sections.h2: Washington County housing at a glance
sections.html: South of Pittsburgh, this big county has about 210,802 residents and 99,340 housing units, and 76.1 percent of households own their homes. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $228,500, a countywide number that masks wide swings. School districts are small and numerous, among them Canon-McMillan, Peters Township, Charleroi, Burgettstown Area and Chartiers-Houston, which means two neighbors across a district line may pay different school taxes. Name the district in your listing, and price from recent sales inside it. With about 37.8 inches of snow in a typical year, older houses get close scrutiny of the roof and furnace.

Two county offices split the job. County taxes are paid to the Treasurer, 95 W. Beau St., Suite 130, 724-228-6780, whose counter closes at 4:00 p.m. The Tax Revenue Department, in Suite 525 at 724-228-6850, handles both assessments and delinquent claims.

For delinquent taxes the Treasurer refuses personal checks. Cash, cards, money orders and certified checks work. Online payment carries a fee of 2.50 percent on cards with a $2.00 minimum, or $1.50 per electronic check.

If back taxes sit on the house you are selling, get a written balance from Tax Revenue before closing so the title company can pay it out of your proceeds. A Board of Assessment Appeals exists too, and Tax Revenue can explain how to file.

sections.h2: Steps from signed deed to recorded deed
sections.html:
Most sales follow one sequence. A title company or attorney drafts the deed and the Statement of Value, you sign at closing, and the settlement agent totals the transfer tax and recording charges. Then the deed travels to the recorder, on paper ahead of the cutoff or electronically, and gets indexed and scanned that day.

In the days before closing, count the pages, the names to index and the parcel numbers, since those three drive the extras in the fee table. Ask whether recording will happen on closing day or the next business day. A cash sale skips the lender paperwork, but recording works identically and the same fees and transfer tax apply.

Bring a photo ID to closing and keep the recorded copy when it comes back. If anything about the deed is unclear, such as how many parcels it covers or whether an exemption form is needed, phone the recorder at 724-228-6806 first. A rejected filing costs a day, and a day can matter when a buyer's loan is waiting to fund.

faqs.q: What time does the Washington County recorder stop accepting deeds?
faqs.a: Recording stops at 4:00 p.m., thirty minutes ahead of closing time. The office is at 95 W. Beau St., Suite 520, Washington, and a late deed waits until the next business day.

faqs.q: Can I record a legal-size deed electronically in Washington County?
faqs.a: No. The county no longer accepts legal-size pages electronically. Letter-size pages need at least 12 point type and legal-size pages need at least 14 point, so bring a paper original if the document is on legal paper.

faqs.q: Does a Washington County deed fee cover extra pages and names?
faqs.a: The base fee covers four pages, four indexed names and one PIN. Pages past four cost $2.00 apiece, names $0.50 and PINs $10.00, and the CJEA surcharge rose by $1. Call 724-228-6806 for the exact total.

faqs.q: How can I look up recorded deeds in Washington County, PA?
faqs.a: Search Landex online, which covers 1781 to today, or sit at a public terminal inside the office.

faqs.q: Who owes transfer tax on a Washington County sale?
faqs.a: Both. The state takes 1 percent of the transfer value from buyer and seller jointly, and a local tax usually comes with it. Your contract assigns the cost, and the recorder can quote the local rate.
